arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Banker argued tribes lack inherent sovereign power over nonmembers.
Mr. Gannon argued tribes retain legitimate civil authority over nonmember land.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned the practical enforcement of tribal taxes.
Justice Ginsburg compared tax collection to a gas station scenario.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Plains Commerce Bank seeks to avoid tribal court jurisdiction. The Long Family Land and Cattle Company wants the tribe to collect taxes from the bank.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of tribal authority over nonmember businesses. It determines whether tribes can enforce tax laws against outside entities. The outcome shapes the balance of power between tribal and state governments.
